title: Run workflows on their schedule in `serve` and `once`
body:
## Summary

Each poll now reads `.linewright/workflows/` on the default branch and starts the workflows that are due. The due rule sits in the reconcile step, so a single function applies the `max-workers` ceiling to pipeline runs and workflow runs together.

```
Factory::cycle
├─ store.snapshot(...)
├─ self.workflows()            list_files + parse; a file that does not parse is logged and skipped
├─ reconcile(snapshot, live, Workflows { defined, last_runs, in_flight }, now, policy)
│   ├─ pipeline starts         room = max-workers − pipeline runs − workflow runs in flight
│   └─ schedule(..., room left)
│        due ⇔ next tick after last run ≤ now ∧ no run in flight
│        first seen ⇒ recorded as run now, no run
│        → RunWorkflow(w)…, then RecordLastRuns(..) if the record changed
└─ execute
    ├─ RunWorkflow      spawns the same run `workflow run NAME` starts; a run that fails is logged
    └─ RecordLastRuns   <work-dir>/workflow-runs.json, written to a temp file then renamed into place
```

- **The record:** it is written to `<work-dir>/workflow-runs.json`, survives a restart and never goes to GitHub. `workflow run NAME` leaves it alone.
- **Replay:** it sets `schedule_workflows = false`, so no workflow runs.
- **Store:** it gains `list_files(branch, dir)`, backed by `git ls-tree` locally and the contents API on GitHub.
- **Priority:** workflow runs get the room the pipeline's runs leave, since no person is waiting on them.
- **Order:** the record is written after the runs start. A stop between the two leaves the workflow due again after a restart, rather than recording a run that never started.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `a_workflow_runs_on_the_first_poll_after_its_schedule_ticks` failed: `left: 0, right: 1` workflow sessions.
  **After:** `cargo test --locked` passes, including:
  - `tests/reconcile.rs`, the due rule:
    - ticked since the last run → run plus record
    - not yet due → nothing
    - first seen → record only
    - five missed ticks → one run
    - in flight → nothing, then one run once it ends
    - the ceiling, with workflows getting the room the pipeline leaves
    - first seen with no room → still recorded
  - `tests/workflow_schedule.rs`, end to end with the fake clock:
    - runs on the poll after a tick
    - first seen does not run
    - five hours stopped, then a restart → one run, and the record is under the work directory
    - a file that does not parse is skipped and the other workflow runs
    - with `max-workers` 1 the run waits for the implementer
    - `workflow run` by hand leaves the schedule as it was
  - `tests/replay.rs`: `a_replay_runs_no_workflows`, with the clock moved past a tick mid-replay. It fails if replay leaves scheduling on.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy`, `test` and `doc` all pass with warnings denied.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The only new state is a local bookkeeping file under the work directory.

**Blast Radius:** moderate

- Every `serve` and `once` poll now makes one extra GitHub request to list the workflow directory, plus one per workflow file.
- Workflow runs share `max-workers` with the pipeline.
- Repositories with no `.linewright/workflows/` see no other change.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Closes #7

nodes.body:
> *Linewright, update*

Merged `origin/main` into the branch. There was one conflict, in `src/factory.rs`.

- **What main changed:** a workflow run now files the issues its result returns, as the machine user, instead of only logging them. Main also took `issues` out of the `workflow run finished` log line.
- **What this branch had done:** it moved that log line out of `Factory::run_workflow` into `run_and_log`, so that `workflow run NAME` and scheduled runs share it.
- **How it was resolved:** I kept the branch's `Factory::workflows` and made main's log change inside `run_and_log`. Both paths go through `run::workflow`, so a scheduled run now files its issues just as a run by hand does. I also updated the doc comment on `run_and_log` to say it files the issues.

`cargo fmt`, `clippy --all-targets`, `test` and `doc` all pass with warnings denied, including `workflow_run.rs` (15 tests), `workflow_schedule.rs` (6), `reconcile.rs` (35) and `replay.rs` (3).

> *Linewright, review*

CI is green: ready for review.

> *Linewright, rework*

Rebased the branch on the latest `main` (`bdbe4b3`, *File the issues a workflow run returns*) and dropped the merge commit. The branch is now one commit on top of `main`:

```
* b74a3e1 Run workflows on their schedule in `serve` and `once`
* bdbe4b3 File the issues a workflow run returns   ← origin/main
```

- **Conflict:** the only one was in `src/factory.rs`. I resolved it the same way the merge did: main's change to the log line goes inside `run_and_log`, and the branch's `Factory::workflows` stays. The rebased tree is byte-for-byte the same as the merge commit `4d5dc39` (`git diff 4d5dc39 HEAD` is empty), so no code changed.
- **Commit message:** it now also says that a scheduled run is the same run `workflow run NAME` starts, so it files the issues its result returns too. On top of the new `main`, that holds from this commit on.
- **Checks:** `cargo fmt`, then `clippy --all-targets`, `test` and `doc`, all with warnings denied, pass on the rebased commit. That includes `workflow_schedule.rs` (6 tests), `workflow_run.rs` (15), `reconcile.rs` (35) and `replay.rs` (3).

This rewrites the branch's history, so the push has to be a force-push.
